newsitem.title: USA: Fed Chairman Greenspan to wed television reporter.
newsitem.headline: Fed Chairman Greenspan to wed television reporter.

text.p: U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan and NBC television reporter Andrea Mitchell have become engaged and plan to get married in the new year, a central bank spokesman said on Tuesday.
Known for his cautious steering of interest rate policy as head of the powerful Fed, Greenspan proposed to Mitchell on Christmas Day after the two had dated for more than a decade.
"We have a huge amount in common. It's a really great match," Greenspan told the Washington Post newspaper.
Greenspan, who is 70, and Mitchell, who is 20 years his junior, were both married previously.
Mitchell told the Post the proposal, which came after the two had spent Christmas morning with friends, was a complete surprise.
"We came home and he said, "Do you want a big wedding or a small wedding?'" she recounted.
Asked what effect the news of their engagement might have on Wall Street, Mitchell replied, "I hope they will not become irrationally exuberant."
Greenspan rocked world financial markets earlier this month when he said that the central bank had to be wary when "irrational exuberance" infected Wall Street stock prices.
